title: Accounts Assistant
description:
Accounts Assistant

Cosgrove & Cosgrove Ltd Telford, Shropshire

£28,000-£30,000 per annum depending on experience Full-time Permanent Office-based

Cosgrove & Cosgrove is looking for an experienced Accounts Assistant to join our small finance team in Telford, supporting the day-to-day accounts across multiple businesses.

This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys keeping accurate records, resolving queries and taking ownership of their work. You should be confident completing bank reconciliations independently and managing a varied workload without constant supervision.

What you'll be doing
- Completing bank reconciliations independently across multiple accounts and investigating discrepancies.
- Maintaining purchase and sales ledgers, processing supplier invoices, and raising and processing sales invoices.
- Processing expenses and credit card transactions, matching receipts and following up missing information.
- Using Dext to support invoice and receipt processing.
- Carrying out bookkeeping and data entry, keeping QuickBooks Online records accurate and up to date.
- Preparing and posting journals, including payroll journals, and collating payroll information.
- Liaising with colleagues and suppliers to resolve queries.
- Supporting month-end tasks and the wider finance team.

What we're looking for
- At least two years' practical UK accounts or bookkeeping experience.
- The ability to complete bank reconciliations independently.
- Practical experience of purchase and sales ledgers, supplier invoices and expenses.
- Good Excel skills and practical experience using QuickBooks Online. Both are essential.
- Strong attention to detail, good organisation and the ability to prioritise your workload.
- A reliable commute to our Telford office for this fully office-based role.

Experience using Dext would be an advantage. An AAT qualification or progress towards one would be useful, but is not essential; practical experience and the ability to do the work are what matter.

How to apply

Please submit your CV and include a short covering note answering the following:
- How many years of practical UK accounts or bookkeeping experience do you have?
- How many years have you used QuickBooks Online, and have you used Dext?
- What experience do you have of preparing payroll information and posting payroll journals?
- How would you describe your Excel level? Please give examples of the functions or tasks you use regularly.
- What are you looking for in your next role and why are you leaving your current position? If you are not currently employed, please tell us what you are looking for next.
- What is your notice period or earliest available start date?

title: Customer Service Administrator
description:
Role Details

Role: Property Manager

Location: Shrewsbury

Salary: £28,000-£31,000

Role Overview

Durrant Talent Solutions is proud to be partnering with a leading national residential managing agent in the search for a Property Manager to join their Shrewsbury team.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced Property Manager to take ownership of a residential portfolio, delivering exceptional property management services while building strong relationships with leaseholders, residents, clients and contractors.

The successful candidate will be responsible for ensuring developments are managed to the highest professional standards, maintaining compliance, overseeing maintenance and service delivery, and providing an outstanding customer experience across their portfolio.

Role Responsibilities
- Manage a portfolio of residential leasehold developments.
- Build and maintain strong relationships with leaseholders, Resident Management Companies (RMCs), Right to Manage Companies (RTMs) and freeholder clients.
- Prepare and manage annual service charge budgets in conjunction with internal teams.
- Monitor expenditure and ensure developments are managed within approved budgets.
- Arrange, attend and chair site inspections and client meetings as required.
- Instruct, monitor and review contractors to ensure works are completed to the required standard.
- Oversee planned and reactive maintenance across the portfolio.
- Ensure compliance with all relevant health and safety legislation, including fire, asbestos, water hygiene and lift regulations.
- Work closely with internal departments including finance, compliance and customer services.
- Respond promptly and professionally to customer enquiries and resolve issues effectively.
- Ensure accurate property records are maintained and all administration is completed within agreed timescales.

Essential Experience

The successful candidate will have:
- Previous experience managing a residential block management portfolio.
- A good understanding of residential leasehold legislation and property management best practice.
- Excellent communication and relationship-building skills.
- Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage a varied workload.
- A proactive and customer-focused approach.
- The ability to prioritise tasks and work independently.
- Competent IT skills, including Microsoft Office.
- A full UK driving licence (where required).

Desirable Experience
- TPI qualified or working towards level 3
- Experience using property management software such as Qube, TRAMPS, Propman or similar.

Equal Opportunities Statement

Durrant Talent Solutions is committed to promoting equality, diversity and inclusion throughout the recruitment process. We welcome applications from all suitably qualified individuals regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected under the Equality Act 2010. Selection decisions are based solely on skills, experience, qualifications and suitability for the role.

Due to the high volume of applications received, we may only be able to contact candidates who are shortlisted. If you do not hear from us within 7 days of submitting your application, please assume your application has been unsuccessful on this occasion.

title: Housing Repairs Administrator
description:
Housing Repairs Administrator

Location: Gosport, Hampshire, PO12 3 BE
Salary: Circa £30,000 per annum, FTE
Contract: Part time, Permanent 25 hours per week

Keep homes running. Keep residents happy. Make a difference every day.

Are you organised, practical and great with people

Do you enjoy coordinating workloads, solving problems and making sure things happen when they should

We're looking for a Housing Repairs Administrator to join our Property Services team and play a vital role in delivering a responsive, reliable and customer-focused repairs service for our residents.

This is a varied and rewarding role that combines administration, scheduling, customer service and practical property maintenance knowledge. You'll be the key link between residents reporting repairs, maintenance operatives carrying out work and contractors supporting the service.

No two days are the same. One moment you'll be coordinating urgent repair appointments and managing workloads, the next you'll be speaking with residents, updating repair records or helping colleagues resolve operational challenges.

If you enjoy working in a fast-paced environment where organisation, communication and problem-solving skills make a genuine difference, we'd love to hear from you.

About the Role

As our Housing Repairs Administrator, you'll help ensure repairs are completed efficiently, appointments are managed effectively and residents receive excellent service throughout the repairs process.

You'll coordinate maintenance activities from initial report through to completion, ensuring jobs are correctly allocated, records are maintained and residents remain informed every step of the way.

This role is ideal for someone who understands property maintenance and enjoys combining practical knowledge with administration and customer service responsibilities.

What You'll Be Doing
- Coordinating Repairs and Maintenance
- Receiving and processing repair requests from residents.
- Scheduling routine, urgent and emergency maintenance work.
- Monitoring outstanding repairs and ensuring work progresses within agreed timescales.
- Arranging follow-on works, contractor visits and additional appointments where required.
- Maintaining accurate repair records and updating systems throughout the lifecycle of each job.
- Supporting Residents
- Acting as a key point of contact for residents regarding repairs and appointments.
- Keeping residents informed about progress, delays or changes to scheduled works.
- Responding professionally and empathetically to enquiries and concerns.
- Helping ensure vulnerable residents receive the support and communication they need.
- Using your maintenance knowledge to help identify repair requirements and allocate work appropriately.
- Liaising with operatives and contractors regarding access, materials and scheduling.
- Supporting the wider maintenance team to ensure repairs are completed efficiently.
- Providing practical assistance with maintenance tasks when appropriate and within your level of competence.
- Producing information and reports relating to repair activity and performance.
- Identifying opportunities to improve scheduling, communication and service delivery.

About You

You'll be a highly organised and proactive individual who enjoys balancing customer service with operational coordination.

You will have:
- Previous experience in a repairs, maintenance, construction, property services or similar environment.
- Practical maintenance knowledge and an understanding of common property repairs.
- Experience coordinating workloads, appointments or operational activities.
- Strong administration and organisational skills.
- Confidence using IT systems and Microsoft Office applications, particularly Outlook, Word and Excel.
- Excellent communication skills and the ability to build positive relationships with residents, contractors and colleagues.
- A calm and professional approach when dealing with changing priorities and challenging situations.

It Would Be Great If You Also Have
- Experience within social housing repairs and maintenance.
- Experience scheduling maintenance operatives or trade teams.
- Knowledge of responsive repairs, void properties or planned maintenance programmes.
- Experience using housing management, repairs management or workforce scheduling systems.
- Relevant qualifications in housing, construction, maintenance or administration.

Why Join Us

This is an opportunity to join an organisation where the work you do has a direct impact on residents' homes and wellbeing.

You'll become part of a supportive team that values collaboration, practical problem-solving and excellent customer service. You'll have the chance to use both your organisational skills and maintenance knowledge in a role that offers genuine variety and responsibility.

Every repair coordinated, every appointment managed and every problem resolved helps ensure residents receive the quality service they deserve.

Interested

If you're looking for a role where you can combine administration, customer service and practical maintenance knowledge while making a meaningful difference to residents every day, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply now and help us deliver a repairs service that residents can rely on

title: Payroll Assistant
description:
Role: Payroll Assistant

Location: West Midlands - Hybrid (1 day a week)

Duration: 3 Months

Hourly rate: up to £17.24 + Holiday per hour

Full Time: 36 hours per week

Sellick Partnership are currently recruiting for a Payroll Assistant to join our reputable public sector organisation based in West Midlands. This is a contract for 3 months, with a possibility to be extended, and is offered on a hybrid basis with a minimum of 1 day a week in the office.

The duties of the Payroll Assistant will include:
- Processing weekly and monthly payroll information
- Inputting employee data, including starters, leavers and contract changes
- Recording overtime, bonuses, commission payments and deductions
- Calculating statutory payments such as sick pay, maternity pay and paternity pay
- Checking timesheets and attendance records for accuracy
- Maintaining employee payroll records and personnel files
- Processing pension contributions and benefit deductions
- Responding to employee payroll queries and resolving discrepancies
- Producing payroll reports for management and finance teams
- Ensuring compliance with payroll legislation and company policies
- Submitting payroll data to HMRC and other relevant bodies
- Reconciling payroll reports and identifying any errors before payment runs
- Assisting with year-end payroll activities, including P60s and P11 Ds where required

The Payroll Assistant ideally should:
- Have a minimum of 2 years payroll experience
- Be educated to GCSE mathematics or equivalent
- Have experience in a similar level
- Have knowledge and understanding of current payroll legislation
- Have knowledge of statutory legislation including taxation, NI, SSP, SMP, SPP and P45s and P46s

The Payroll Assistant will need to have excellent communication skills and effectively be able to communicate to stakeholders of all levels. Furthermore, the ideal candidate will have an impeccable eye for detail and accuracy to ensure all workload is carried out effectively and efficiently. They will also need to able to prioritise their workload and be efficient and effective to meet unpredictable deadlines and deal with conflicting demands, whilst working in a high-pressured environment.

If you believe that you are well-suited to this excellent opportunity of Payroll Assistant, please apply directly or contact Charlotte Broomfield at Sellick Partnership for more information. The closing date for CVs is Tuesday 23th October due to the urgent requirement of this role. The closing date may be bought forward should suitable applicants apply.

Sellick Partnership is proud to be an inclusive and accessible recruitment business and we support applications from candidates of all backgrounds and circumstances. Please note, our advertisements use years' experience, hourly rates, and salary levels purely as a guide and we assess applications based on the experience and skills evidenced on the CV. For information on how your personal details may be used by Sellick Partnership, please review our data processing notice on our website.

title: Administrator - Data Entry Project
salary_text: £12.71 - £13 per hour (Immediate start and great training)
description:
Are you available to start a temporary data entry project ASAP?

We're looking for someone to support a busy data cleansing and administration project for a business based in Telford, specifically within the TF1 area, as they prepare for the implementation of a brand-new HR system in February.

There is a huge volume of employee data and physical documentation that needs to be reviewed, cleansed, updated and organised ahead of the changeover. You'll be supporting the team with a variety of data entry and general administration tasks, including scanning documents, logging information, organising paperwork, securely destroying documents where required and updating employee records.

This would be a fantastic opportunity for a graduate or school leaver looking to gain some valuable office administration experience, or someone who enjoys organised, process-driven work and is happy getting stuck into a busy data entry project.

The role is on a temporary basis, paying 13.00 per hour + holiday accrual, with weekly pay. The position will start ASAP and is expected to be ongoing, with the potential for around five months of work and possibly the opportunity to support the business further during the transition to its new HR system.

The hours are Monday to Friday, 8:30am-5:00pm, with a one-hour lunch break. Due to the nature of the project and the volume of physical paperwork involved, this will be a fully office-based position in Telford.

Please note that due to the type of project this is, the successful candidate will be required to sign an NDA before commencing any work.

What does the day-to-day look like?

This is a very admin-heavy, data entry-focused project, supporting the business in getting its employee records and documentation ready for a major HR system change.

You'll be scanning and logging documents, organising physical records, updating employee information, cleansing existing data and ensuring everything is accurate, up to date and ready for the transition. You'll need to be comfortable carrying out repetitive tasks and working through a high volume of information, with accuracy and attention to detail being key.

What do we need from you?
- Good attention to detail and the ability to work accurately with data and documentation.
- Basic computer skills and a willingness to learn new systems and processes.
- A proactive attitude and the ability to get stuck into a busy, hands-on administration project.
- Someone who is comfortable with repetitive data entry and document management tasks.
- The ability to start ASAP and commit to an ongoing temporary assignment.
- The ability to commute easily to the Telford TF1 area, as the role is fully office-based.

Previous office administration experience would be beneficial, but it's certainly not essential. We'd be very happy to hear from graduates, school leavers or anyone looking to gain valuable experience in an office environment.

What next?

If you're available to start ASAP and think this could be a good fit, apply for the role or get in touch with Bobby to find out more. We're keen to speak with candidates as soon as possible, with a view to getting someone started ASAP.

Looking for the next step in your career? Think Specialist Recruitment.

Think Specialist Recruitment is an independent support staff recruitment agency based in Hemel Hempstead and working across the Herts, Beds and Bucks area. We specialise in permanent and temporary recruitment, with areas of expertise including administration, customer service/call centre, PA/secretarial, human resources, accountancy and finance, sales admin/sales support, marketing and IT Helpdesk/IT support.

description:

title: Project Coordinator
description:
We are recruiting on behalf of a dynamic and growing organisation based in Shropshire that is looking for an experienced and highly organised Project Coordinator to join their team. This is a fantastic opportunity to step into a pivotal role within a business that is genuinely ambitious, fast-moving, and invested in the people who help drive it forward.

Working in a hybrid capacity, you will have the flexibility to split your time between the London office and home, while playing a central role in the coordination and delivery of key projects across the business. If you are someone who thrives on keeping multiple workstreams on track, communicating clearly with stakeholders, and making sure things get done to the highest standard, this role is for you.

What You Will Be Doing
- Leading the day-to-day coordination of projects from initiation through to successful delivery
- Managing project timelines, milestones, and deliverables, ensuring deadlines are consistently met
- Facilitating project meetings, capturing actions, and holding teams accountable for progress
- Maintaining comprehensive project documentation, risk registers, and status reports
- Acting as a central point of contact between internal teams, senior stakeholders, and external partners
- Proactively identifying risks, dependencies, and blockers - and escalating or resolving them swiftly
- Supporting resource planning, budget tracking, and reporting as required
- Contributing to the continuous improvement of project management processes and ways of working

What We Are Looking For
- Proven experience in a Project Coordinator, Project Manager, or similar delivery-focused role
- Strong understanding of project management methodologies (e.g. Agile, PRINCE2, or similar)
- Exceptional organisational skills with the ability to manage competing priorities across multiple projects
- Confident communicator - able to engage effectively with stakeholders at all levels, including senior leadership
- Proficient in project management tools such as Jira, Asana, MS Project, or equivalent
- A proactive, solutions-focused mindset with excellent attention to detail
- Comfortable working independently in a hybrid environment
- A relevant project management qualification (e.g. PRINCE2, APM, PMP) is desirable but not essential

What Is On Offer
- Hybrid working - a flexible split between the London office and home
- 28 days annual leave plus bank holidays
- A high-profile role with genuine influence over project outcomes and business direction
- Fantastic opportunities to grow within the organisation, with clear pathways for career progression
- Funded training and support for professional development and project management qualifications
- A collaborative, ambitious team culture where your contribution is recognised and rewarded

This organisation is recruiting directly through Consula, their recruitment partner.

title: Stores Coordinator / Front Counter Support
description:
Stores Coordinator / Front counter Support
Location: Telford
Pay Rate: From 12.71 per hour, with more available for the right candidate
Contract: Temporary to Permanent Monday-Friday 08:30-17:00
Start Date: ASAP
Pertemps are currently recruiting for a reliable, presentable and customer-focused Stores Coordinator to join our client's team on a temp-to-perm basis.
This is a varied, hands-on role combining stores duties, order picking, purchase order administration and front counter customer service. You will be dealing directly with tradespeople at the front counter, assisting with their requirements and developing your product knowledge to help customers find the right products for their needs.
Key Responsibilities of this Stores Coordinator / Front counter Support role:
- Managing stores duties and keeping stock organised.
- Picking and preparing customer orders accurately.
- Raising and processing purchase orders (POs).
- Providing front desk support and serving customers at the counter.
- Dealing professionally with tradespeople and assisting with product enquiries.
- Learning the company's products to confidently advise customers and support sales.
- Assisting with deliveries and collections, including driving a 3.5-tonne van when required.
- Maintaining a clean, tidy and organised working environment.

The Ideal Candidate for this Stores Coordinator / Front counter Support position:
- Presentable, professional and confident when dealing with customers.
- Computer literate, with good administration skills.
- Experience working in Stores (Stock control, picking products, Goods in/out, Inputting data)
- Reliable, organised and able to work on their own initiative.
- Willing to learn about products and develop their sales knowledge.
- Holds a full UK driving licence and is comfortable driving a 3.5-tonne van.
- Previous experience in stores, warehouse operations, trade counter sales or a similar role would be advantageous.
- A valid forklift licence (Counterbalance)

What's on Offer?
- Starting pay from 12.71 per hour, with flexibility for the right candidate.
- A temporary-to-permanent opportunity for someone looking for a long-term position.
- The chance to develop product knowledge and build a career within the business.
- A varied role combining customer service, administration and practical stores work.

If this ticks you boxes, please apply now or contact Ellie in our Telford branch!

title: Receptionist/Administrator
description: We are looking for an enthusiastic, reliable and patient-focused Receptionist/Administrator to join our friendly GP practice team. The successful candidate will work as part of our reception team, supporting the safe and efficient preparation and supply of medicines to our patients. You will play an important role in ensuring that prescriptions are processed accurately, medicines are appropriately stored and stock levels are maintained. This is a busy and varied role, requiring excellent attention to detail, good organisational skills and a professional approach to patient care. Previous experience in a reception, office administration or GP practice environment would be advantageous. However, we are also interested in candidates with relevant transferable experience and a willingness to undertake appropriate training. The successful candidate will: Provide a friendly, professional and welcoming reception service to patients and visitors. Answer telephone calls and deal with patient enquiries promptly and courteously, ensuring queries are directed to the appropriate member of the practice team. Book, amend and cancel appointments in accordance with practice procedures. Support patients with general administrative and non-clinical queries.. Register new patients and maintain accurate patient records. Undertake general administrative duties, including scanning, filing, processing correspondence and updating records. Support clinicians and the wider practice team with day-to-day administrative tasks. Liaise with hospitals, pharmacies, community services and other healthcare organisations where appropriate. Maintain confidentiality and ensure patient information is handled securely and in accordance with practice policies and information governance requirements. Follow practice procedures relating to safeguarding, health and safety, infection prevention and confidentiality. Work effectively as part of a busy multidisciplinary team and contribute to the smooth running of the practice. Deal with patients in a respectful, sensitive and professional manner, including those who may be distressed or have additional needs. Undertake other reasonable administrative duties appropriate to the role. To provide a friendly, professional and efficient reception and administrative service to patients and visitors, supporting the smooth day-to-day operation of the practice. The post holder will work as part of the wider practice team, providing front-line support to patients, managing appointments and enquiries, maintaining accurate patient information and undertaking a range of administrative duties in accordance with practice policies, procedures and information governance requirements. The post holder will work within the limits of their training and competence and will refer clinical, complex or sensitive matters to the appropriate member of the practice team.
